## 5. Plumbing — configured but dead

All bucket 5 unless noted. None of these is a token finding.

### 5.1 Confirmed

**PLUMB-F-10 — the rollout gate (read this first).** Both v0.10 recorders demonstrably work: `payment-gateway-ms/.claude/claudehut/state/decc1bd2-*.rules-loaded.jsonl` is 124,852 B / 706 well-formed rows and the matching `.dispatches.jsonl` has 15. Both events are new in 0.10.0 (`hooks/hooks.json:64-77`; the 0.9.1 cache copy contains neither). The near-empty ledgers are **entirely explained by rollout**: 15 project-scoped installs, only 2 on 0.10.0.
**Narrowings:** 0.10.0 merged 2026-08-11 and today is 2026-08-17, so much of "13 of 15 stale" is six-day release recency. The genuine chronic tail is **5 installs on 0.8.0 or older that never updated**: wallet-ms 0.2.0 (2026-06-03), bank-ms 0.5.1, auth-ms 0.6.0, core-ledger-ms and payment-orchestrator-ms 0.8.0. Drop the superlative "largest configured-but-does-nothing mechanism" — that ranking was not measured.
**The in-plugin half of the fix is unworkable, not merely incomplete** (see front matter). **Only the second half survives: install at user scope, or adopt an external `claude plugin update` habit.**

**PLUMB-F-01 — `record-failure.sh` reads a `tool_error` object that does not exist.** See §4.4; the remedy is `.error`/`.is_interrupt`/`.duration_ms` and **not** `.error_type`/`.is_timeout`.

**PLUMB-F-02 — `SubagentStop` `agent_type` carries the caller-supplied `name`, so every named dispatch skips its file contract.** `scripts/verify-subagent.sh:28` strips only the `claudehut:` prefix and then matches four literals at `:32,:37,:42,:58`; a named dispatch falls to the `*)` no-op at `:76`. Proven by a 1:1 join: transcript `decc1bd2-*.jsonl` holds 15 Agent `tool_use` calls each with `subagent_type="claudehut:claudehut-<x>"` AND `name="<instance>"`, and the same session's `.dispatches.jsonl` holds exactly those 15 `name` values in order and never a `subagent_type`. Scale: **459 claudehut dispatches, 123 named** (26.8%) — reuse-scanner 7 named of 10, plan-reviewer 9 of 68, planner 2 of 13, learner 2 of 42. Every eval fixture (`gate-tests.sh:200-227`, `conformance.sh:545-556`) feeds the bare or plugin-scoped name, a form production sends only 73% of the time.
**Mechanically proven for SubagentStop, not merely inferred:** `_W`'s finally block emits `NDe(...,le,tt,void 0,e.agentType)` (@280407908) and SubagentStart emits `Tjn(r,le,e.agentType,...)` (@280397959) — the same `agentDefinition` field; and when `name` is supplied the AgentTool routes to `spawnTeammate({name:i, agent_type:t, ...})`, whose in-process runner synthesises `O={agentType:t.agentName, …}` (@282101655). So `e.agentType` **is** the caller-supplied name.
**Both proposed fixes are defective as written.** (i) The SubagentStart payload is only `{…session fields, hook_event_name, agent_id, agent_type}` — **there is no `subagent_type` field on that event**, and `agent_id` for these dispatches is literally `<name>@session-<sid>`, i.e. name-derived. `record-dispatch.sh` cannot write an `agent_id → subagent_type` row. **The event carrying both is `PreToolUse` on the Agent tool** (`tool_input.subagent_type` + `tool_input.name`); `hooks/hooks.json` currently has PreToolUse matchers only for `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` and `Skill`, so the fix needs a new `Agent` matcher recording `name → subagent_type`. (ii) The interim pattern list (`*reuse-scan*`, `*plan-review*`, `*learner*`) silently drops `claudehut-planner` (13 dispatches), and `*plan*` would swallow plan-reviewer, so arms must be disjoint or plan-review-first. Since names are caller-chosen free text, glob matching can **false-block** an unrelated agent — the PreToolUse join is the fix, not a co-equal option.
**Scope note:** all 15 named dispatches returned `status:"teammate_spawned"` — async in-process teammates, not synchronous subagents. Fixing the string match restores the block, but the workflow assumption that the main thread *waits* for the artifact does not automatically return.
**Version caveat:** the binary's own docs describe `agent_type` as "Agent type name (e.g. general-purpose, code-reviewer)", so name-in-`agent_type` is an undocumented artifact of the named route and may shift between Claude Code versions — an argument for keying on something stable rather than patching the string match.

**RES-H3 — `hooks/hooks.json:5` omits the `fork` SessionStart matcher.** The docs list five values (`startup, resume, clear, compact, fork`); `:5` is `"startup|resume|clear|compact"`. Local install is 2.1.233, past the `v2.1.214` cutoff at which forks began reporting `source: fork` rather than `resume` — so this is a **recent regression**, not a longstanding hole. **This is the same finding as PLUMB-F-09 [unverified], which is superseded by it.**
**Definitely lost on a fork:** the digest additionalContext, the learnings injection + `.injected.json` snapshot, the plane-init fallback (`bootstrap.sh:21-23`), rule-template migration (`:47-54`), and the Summer-KB install/self-heal/grounding block (`:97-118`). **Overstated: "no workflow injection"** — a fork inherits the parent transcript, so digest text already injected in the parent is still present.
**The severe branch is conditional and [unverified]:** if a fork gets a new `session_id`, no `state/$sid.json` is ever written (`bootstrap.sh:39-41` is the sole writer) and `gate-write.sh` fails open (`:6-7`) for the **entire** forked session. The docs do not state fork's session_id behaviour.
**"One token in hooks.json:5" is FALSE and the naive fix is a regression.** On a fork with a fresh sid there is also no `$sid.snapshot.json` (snapshots are keyed to the parent's sid), so `:35-37` cannot restore and `:39` fires `set-phase discover`, which per its own comment "also resets the skill rail". A user who forks mid-implement lands at `phase=discover` with the rail closed and their next production write denied — exactly the hazard the author documented at `bootstrap.sh:31-34`. State cannot be inherited either: **no hook payload carries a parent-session-id field.**
**Correct fix:** add `|fork` AND make `bootstrap.sh` read the `source` field (it does not today) and skip the `set-phase discover` re-arm when `source=="fork"`. Ship with a real `--fork-session` test that first settles whether the sid changes. Also fix the stale comment at `bootstrap.sh:2` ("matcher: startup|clear|compact" — it already omits `resume`).

### 5.2 Unverified

- **PLUMB-F-04 [unverified]** — the `UserPromptExpansion` matcher `implement|discover|brainstorm` at `hooks/hooks.json:20` **can never match**. The runtime matches it against `command_name`, and because the string is pure alnum+pipe it takes the **exact-string list** branch, not the regex branch — so `command_name` must literally equal one of the three. Plugin skills always arrive namespaced (`claudehut:brainstorm` observed 3×; `/claudehut:claudehut-init` 10×). The 67 bare `<command-name>implement</command-name>` hits are **not** slash invocations — each is followed by "Base directory for this skill: …/skills/implement" inside an `isSidechain` subagent transcript, i.e. the `agents/claudehut-implementer.md` `skills:` preload. **Fix:** drop the matcher (the script already no-ops on non-claudehut names at `:34-37`) or set `claudehut:.*` — the colon forces the regex branch.
  **Consequence (the Q5 wedge):** `gate-write.sh:150-154` requires `implement_skill_ok`, set only by `record-skill.sh` on `PreToolUse(Skill)`. A user typing `/claudehut:implement` does not go through the Skill tool, so the rail stays closed — and `record-skill-expansion.sh`, written specifically to close that hole (`:5-9`), never fires. **The wedge it was built to fix is still open.** 86 production occurrences of that deny string exist, but they cannot be attributed to slash-invokers specifically — treat 86 as an upper bound. Confirmed working alongside it: `record-skill.sh` reads `.tool_input.skill` correctly (204 production Skill calls) and `bin/claudehut-state:397` strips the namespace, so the Skill-tool path does open the rail (67 state files carry `implement_skill_ok=true`).
- **PLUMB-F-05 [unverified]** — all **11** distinct `mcp__*` tool names declared across `agents/` are unresolvable against the servers actually configured. Configured (`~/.claude.json`): github, memory, sequential-thinking, context7, postgres — **no mysql, no kafka**. The postgres entry is `@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`, whose sole tool is `query`; the live roster exposes exactly `mcp__postgres__query`. The five declared postgres names are real tools on a *different* server (crystaldba/postgres-mcp) — a server/tool-name mismatch, not a non-existent API. **Do not simply swap in `mcp__postgres__query`.** Add a conformance check extracting `mcp__[a-z0-9_-]+__[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` from `agents/*.md` and diffing against a **checked-in inventory snapshot** (not a live connection, or CI fails universally and gets disabled), and record in `templates/mcp-recommendations.md` which server package provides each name. **This check must land before the seven new MCP catalog rows in §6.3.**
- **PLUMB-F-06 [unverified]** — `record-dispatch.sh:25` records `agent_type`, which for named dispatches is the instance label, so the ledger is unjoinable to `agents/*.md`. The single production ledger contains only `explorer-settlement-ft`, `reuse-scan-ft-2`, `rev-db-0088`, `brainstormer-0089`… Same root cause as PLUMB-F-02; same remedy (record the declared type from `PreToolUse(Agent)`), and any such hook must `exit 0` unconditionally or it becomes a new way to block fan-out.
- **PLUMB-F-07 [unverified]** — `bypass=true` disables both gates wholesale, is settable by the model itself via a Bash call with no confirmation and no recorded reason, and **claudehut-state's own model-facing error text advertises it**: `bin/claudehut-state:185` "Use 'set-bypass true' first (recovery mode)" and `:273` "set-bypass true — this unblocks set-plan AND the write gate". **15 of 288 production state files have `bypass=true` (5.2%).** Require `--reason`, persist `bypass_reason`/`bypass_ts`, surface it in gate-done's completion path, and remove the suggestion from model-facing strings (keep it in human docs). Do **not** harden it into a confirmation prompt — bypass is the documented headless escape hatch and that would wedge non-interactive runs.
- **PLUMB-F-08 [unverified, bucket 4]** — `claudehut-implementer` is the only agent declaring a `skills:` preload, pulling the full 12,534 B `implement/SKILL.md` into the subagent window on every spawn (67 dispatches measured). **2,690 B of that (lines 60-95) is a main-thread orchestration section the agent cannot act on** — headed "Main thread only — if you have no Agent tool, skip this section" at `:74`, and at `:84` instructing the agent to dispatch itself. Move it to `references/orchestration.md` (which already exists and is already referenced at `:76`) and leave a one-line pointer. **Bucket-4 trim — saves nothing in the main thread; the justification is that the section actively misleads the agent.** The mandatory pointer at `:76` must stay or main-thread parallel-dispatch discipline regresses.
- **PLUMB-F-11 [unverified]** — the fast-lane file-count bound counts only the **first** path of a write batch. `gate-write.sh:30` takes `head -1` of the extracted path list and `fastlane_bound_ok` (`:129-141`) unions git-tracked-modified + untracked with that single `$rel`. New files created in the same batch are neither tracked-modified nor yet on disk, so a batch can pass a cap of 2 while touching more. The exemption loop directly above (`:60-96`) correctly iterates the **full** list — the inconsistency is confined to the fast-lane bound. 81 "fast lane denied" occurrences in transcripts, so the path is live. Fixing it makes the fast lane stricter; the cap may need raising from 2.
- **Data-hygiene note [unverified]** — one production state file carries `profile=opus+xhigh`, not a valid profile value; `set-profile` appears to accept unvalidated input. 1 of 288 — too small to file, but worth a validation arm.

---

## 6. New features — proposals

Clearly labelled proposals, not findings.

### 6.1 Core proposals

**IDEA-F2 — `micro` tier below `trivial` for comment/doc-only diffs.** *(M)*
- **What:** today the cheapest path still pays the digest, a reuse-scan artifact, the implement skill and a Review pass. Add a tier the gate can verify from the diff shape that skips the reuse-scan **dispatch** entirely and folds Review into one low-effort reviewer.
- **Files:** `skills/claudehut-workflow/references/digest.md:14-20` (tier table); `scripts/gate-write.sh:126-141` (`fastlane_bound_ok`), extended with a diff-shape check (only comment/doc lines changed, nothing under `src/main`) letting that branch skip the rail at `:157`.
- **Win:** removes the reuse-scanner dispatch (~26s measured floor, `evals/bench/BENCH-REPORT.md:19`) and one SKILL.md expansion on the cheapest tasks.
- **Failure mode:** the reuse-scan rail is Law 3 and the gate's only always-on check; carving it out weakens the enforcement story. Mitigate by keeping the rail **unconditional** for anything touching `src/main` — which `gate-write.sh:79` already distinguishes.
- **Test:** `evals/gate-tests.sh` — a comment-only edit under a `micro` state passes with no reuse-scan artifact; the same edit touching `src/main` still denies.

**IDEA-F5 — make the learnings corpus a retrieval index instead of an injected blob.** *(S, bucket 1)*
- **What:** at SessionStart there is no prompt to filter on, so 12 task-agnostic entries are injected unconditionally. Replace with a one-line corpus index, keeping only entries where `inject-learnings.sh:67`'s promoted-and-recurring condition holds (rules that demonstrably did not stick).
- **Files:** `scripts/bootstrap.sh:68` (drop `--top 12` to a summary line). `scripts/inject-phase.sh:54-57` already does the right thing — `--filter "$prompt" --top 5` with `--exclude`.
- **Win:** ~4,731 B off bucket 1 per session start; also removes the recency-decay ordering drift at `inject-learnings.sh:40,55`.
- **Failure mode:** at turn 1 a relevant learning may not surface until turn 2. The promoted-and-recurring carve-out is the safety net for the entries that matter most.
- **Test:** conformance case asserting the SessionStart block is under a byte cap and contains only promoted-and-recurring entries.

**IDEA-F10 — one-line session-hygiene advisory on task completion.** *(S)*
- **What:** the workflow never tells the user the task is durably recorded and the session can be cleared, though clearing is free and a stale session reprocesses its whole context after every pause.
- **Files:** `scripts/gate-done.sh` — a branch on `review==pass` **and** Learn recorded, emitting a top-level `systemMessage` (precedent: `scripts/bootstrap.sh:126`). **Do not put this in `digest.md`** — that is bucket 1, and it would spend per-turn bytes telling the model to do something only the human can do.
- **Win:** converts an idle-gap full-context reprocess into a free fresh session at the one moment clearing is provably safe (Law 6 has persisted everything).
- **Failure mode:** nagging, and a **currently-green eval breaks**: `evals/gate-tests.sh:29` `done_ok()` asserts **empty stdout** on the pass path, with 11 call sites, plus `conformance.sh:603`. Ship the helper rewrite in the same commit. Emit at most once per completed task, never mid-task, never with a non-empty outstanding set.
- **Test:** rewrite `done_ok()` to tolerate a JSON `systemMessage` envelope; assert the advisory appears exactly once and never when `outstanding != []`.

**IDEA-F8 — move the round-invariant auditor payload into the SubagentStart hook.** *(M, bucket 4)*
- **What:** the plugin's own documented roadmap. The rigor contract, enforcement set, pitfalls and vocabulary are identical across every auditor and every round; only the diff hunks differ.
- **Files:** `scripts/record-dispatch.sh:8-15` states the design verbatim. Prompt-side requirement at `skills/review/SKILL.md:78-101`; the file to stop pasting is `skills/review/references/review-rigor.md` (2,911 B).
- **Win:** removes ~2.9 KB of generated **main-thread output** tokens per auditor per round (the main thread's own output stays in its window), plus the same bytes again as subagent input.
- **Failure mode:** named by the hook's own header — a SubagentStart hook has no error surface, so if it silently never fires the auditors lose the rigor contract and **reviews degrade with every eval still green**. Also: `additionalContext` is capped at **10,000 characters**, and the assembled payload measures **5.3–8.3 KB** on real projects (up to ~83% of the cap at report-service-ms, whose LANGUAGE.md is 3,681 B) — one growth step from silently degrading into a file path. Imperative prose in `additionalContext` may also trip prompt-injection defences.
- **Test:** gate the switch on a recorded nonzero dispatch count from IDEA-F7; keep the cat-instruction at `SKILL.md:25-26` until the ledger proves the hook fires. `evals/conformance.sh:314-316` (E3) asserts the skill binds the contract "verbatim" and must be rewritten as part of the change.
- **Correct the multiplier when writing this up:** `review/SKILL.md:146` already scopes re-dispatch to "only the auditors owning a surviving `✗`", so rounds 2–3 are partial. The "18 copies" ceiling is inflated; the real figure is 6 full dispatches plus scoped re-dispatches, and the actual mix is **[unverified — no ledger data]**.

**IDEA-F7 — phase-attributed cost ledger.** *(M, bucket 5)*
- **What:** both v0.10 recorders write per-session sidecars, neither stamps the workflow phase, and nothing reads them.
- **Files:** `scripts/record-dispatch.sh:32-33` (`{ts, agent_type}`) and `scripts/record-rules-loaded.sh:35-36` (`{ts, file_path, load_reason}`) — add `phase`, one `jq` away from `.claude/claudehut/state/$sid.json`, the same file `scripts/inject-phase.sh:23` already reads. Add a `claudehut-state cost` subcommand.
- **Win:** turns the seven-phase walk from an opaque cost into an attributable one.
- **Failure mode:** **[unverified — no ledger data]**; only two ledger files exist across 15 repos, so the recorders' real-world fire rate is not established. **Prove firing (i.e. fix PLUMB-F-10) before building a reader on top.** This complements rather than duplicates `/usage` (RES-M11), which attributes to skills and subagents but knows nothing about claudehut phases. There is also **no export path** from `/usage`'s attribution view, so the two datasets cannot be joined.
- **Test:** `conformance.sh:257` and `:263` currently assert the sidecar fields; extend to assert `phase` is present and resolvable.

**IDEA-F3 — cache the reuse-scan across tasks, keyed on the source tree hash.** *(M)*
- **What:** the reuse *index* is consulted but the *scan* is recomputed from scratch every task, even on an unchanged codebase.
- **Files:** `agents/claudehut-reuse-scanner.md:74`; `templates/reuse-index.json.tmpl:4`. Add `.claude/claudehut/reuse-cache/<hash>.md` keyed on (normalised dimension keywords, `git rev-parse HEAD:src/main`); on a hit, `skills/discover/SKILL.md` writes the cached artifact into `tasks/NNNN-<slug>/reuse-scan.md` and records the flag without dispatching.
- **Win:** removes a full sonnet/high subagent dispatch — the one carrying the `ultrathink` directive — from every repeat task.
- **Failure mode:** a stale verdict is worse than a slow one. Invalidate on any `src/main` tree-hash change; serve only exact dimension matches; a partial match must fall through to a real scan.
- **Test:** eval asserting a second identical task on an unchanged tree produces the artifact with zero reuse-scanner dispatches, and that a one-line `src/main` change forces a real scan.

**IDEA-F11 — cap the review loop by recorded dispatch cost, not round count.** *(S)*
- **What:** `review/SKILL.md:144`'s flat "2 fix→re-spawn rounds" treats a six-auditor round and a two-auditor round as equal.
- **Files:** `skills/review/SKILL.md:144`; budget read from the IDEA-F7 ledger. Keep `:146`'s scoping rule.
- **Win:** makes the most expensive failure mode self-limiting in the currency that matters.
- **Failure mode:** depends on IDEA-F7 producing data. **Also documents an important negative result:** there is no remaining safe parallelism in Review to extract — `:36` already dispatches auditors and the test-runner in ONE message and `:105` runs the refute pass on the main thread with no new dispatch — and agent teams are not the answer (the costs page states they use ~7× more tokens when teammates run in plan mode).
- **Test:** eval asserting the loop halts on budget exhaustion with `set-review capped`, not on a round count.

**IDEA-F6 — anchored slice-reads of reference files.** *(M, bucket 3)*
- **What:** references are read on demand (correct) but read **whole**. Add a section-anchor index to each and teach skills to read only the relevant slice.
- **Files:** the `skills/*/references/*.md` set (235,229 B; largest: `implement/references/testing.md` 12,479 B, `security.md` 11,916 B, `java-lang.md` 11,798 B, `reactive.md` 11,198 B). `skills/review/SKILL.md:137` currently ends "Full matrix: `references/test-matrix.md`" — a whole-file-read instruction.
- **Win:** reduces what enters a window on a read **without removing any bytes** — the only legitimate way to touch bucket 3.
- **Failure mode:** anchors drift from content.
- **Test:** extend `evals/reference-check.sh` to assert every advertised anchor resolves.

**IDEA-F4 — federate reuse index and learnings across the 15 sibling services.** *(L)*
- **What:** `scripts/inject-learnings.sh:36-38` hardcodes one project directory, so payment-gateway-ms's 360 learnings and party-ms's 280 are invisible to siblings that share the same stack, framework and pitfalls — several of which hold zero.
- **Files:** `scripts/inject-learnings.sh:36-38` — add an optional `$CLAUDEHUT_FEDERATION_ROOT` source merged before ranking, with a provenance tag per federated entry.
- **Win:** ~800 recorded learnings become visible to the services that would benefit most.
- **Failure mode:** cross-service noise. Scope federation by the `stack:` convention already used by 18 of 55 rule files, and **hard-cap the federated share of the injected top-N** so bucket 1 does not grow.
- **Test:** eval asserting the federated share never exceeds the cap and that a stack-mismatched entry is excluded.

**IDEA-R2 — a 20-query trigger eval set per phase skill.** *(M)*
- **What:** 8–10 should-trigger and 8–10 should-NOT-trigger queries (the valuable negatives being near-misses that share keywords), 60/40 train/held-out, each query run 3×, best description selected by **test** score to avoid overfitting.
- **Files:** new `evals/trigger-eval/<skill>.json` + a runner alongside `evals/llm-judge.sh`.
- **Win:** turns RES-R1 and SKILL-F6/F7/F8 from style opinions into measured before/after. Near-miss negatives matter most here — 10 skills with heavily overlapping vocabulary.
- **Failure mode:** an LLM-judged eval is noisy; the 3× repetition and held-out split are the mitigations.
- **Test:** the eval is the test; it must be red for at least one current description before it is trusted.

**IDEA-R15 — paired baseline / with-skill runs.** *(L)*
- **What:** spawn two subagents per test case in the **same turn** — one with the skill, one without. Never run the with-skill arm first and collect baselines later. When improving an existing skill, the baseline is a snapshot of the old version.
- **Files:** `evals/run.sh` — add a no-plugin arm per task in `evals/tasks/`, scored by the same judge.
- **Win:** the only rigorous way to land any proposal that **deletes** content, and the only evidence that 68,207 B of skills + 207,364 B of rules beats the model unaided on a Spring task.
- **Failure mode:** doubles eval cost and runtime.
- **Test:** self-evident; require before/after results in the PR for any content-deleting change.

**IDEA-R16 — a single-message acceptance test that the bootstrap actually fires.** *(S)*
- **What:** open a clean session, send exactly one ordinary Java request (e.g. "add a retry to the payment client"), assert `Skill(claudehut:discover)` precedes the first Write/Edit.
- **Files:** new `evals/bootstrap-acceptance.sh`.
- **Win:** the cheapest possible regression test on the highest-consequence single point of failure. The write gate, the skill rail and the profile gate are all dead if the SessionStart hook silently stops firing, and nothing currently detects that.
- **Failure mode:** requires Claude auth, so it is a release-checklist step rather than a CI step (same constraint as `scripts/load-probe.sh`).
- **Test:** it is the test.

**IDEA-DOC1 — fix the six stale MCP tool names in the design doc.** *(S)*
- **What:** v0.10 corrected `templates/mcp-recommendations.md` but `.claude/docs/design/08-mcp-integration.md` was not updated with it. It still documents names that resolve to nothing: `:107` postgres `list_tables`/`describe_table`/`query` (the deprecated server, which the catalog itself calls deprecated at `mcp-recommendations.md:40`); `:144` github `get_pull_request`/`create_issue`/`get_pull_request_status`/`add_pull_request_review` (none exist on the recommended endpoint — the live registry has `pull_request_read`, `issue_write`, `pull_request_review_write`, `list_pull_requests`); `:162` context7 `get-library-docs` (real name `query-docs`); `:235` `mcp__mysql__query` vs the frontmatter's `mcp__mysql__mysql_query`; `:237-241` + `:248` redis and memory entries deleted in v0.10; `:151` the superseded stdio github server.
- **Files:** `.claude/docs/design/08-mcp-integration.md` at `:45-46`, `:77-78`, `:107`, `:144`, `:151`, `:162`, `:227-257`. Also drop the `ask` entries `mcp__postgres__execute_sql_write` / `mcp__mysql__query_write`, neither of which is a real tool name.
- **Win:** this is the exact failure class the plan must not repeat, sitting unfixed. `templates/mcp-recommendations.md:1` points at this doc by name as authoritative, so anyone extending the catalog would propagate `mcp__postgres__query` forward. `agents/*.md:6` already carries the correct names — the drift is doc-only.
- **Failure mode:** none; documentation edit, no behavioural risk.
- **Test:** the PLUMB-F-05 inventory check, extended to `.claude/docs/design/**`.

### 6.2 Native Claude Code levers verified available and unwired

Each verified against primary docs; the caveat column is the part that would bite if adopted naively.

| ID | Lever | Bucket | Caveat that must be respected |
|---|---|---|---|
| RES-H1 | Hook `if` field (permission-rule filter on tool events) | 5 | Per-**handler** key, not a sibling of `matcher`; exactly one rule, **no negation, no list**. Split the PostToolUse group's 2 handlers into 4. Delete only `format-java.sh:12`; **`lint-reuse.sh:23-27` MUST STAY** — its filter is exclusionary (`*Test.java`, `*IT.java`, `*/test/*`, `*/.claude/*`) and inexpressible. Zero token win; only avoided spawns, on handlers already `async:true`. Also drop the obsolete comment at `format-java.sh:4-5` — bare filenames match at any depth. |
| RES-H11 | `statusMessage` on hook entries | 5 | Real Common field, set on none of 13. Worst offenders are `gate-write.sh` (`:30`), `gate-done.sh` (`:60`), `verify-subagent.sh` (`:81`) — no timeout, inheriting the 600s default — **not** bootstrap.sh, already bounded at 15. Whether a spinner renders on SessionStart/Stop is [unverified]. UX only. |
| RES-H7 | `TaskCompleted` / `TaskCreated` can deny a task transition | 5 | **`permissionDecision` does NOT apply** — use exit 2 (TaskCompleted) or exit 2 / top-level `{"decision":"block"}` (TaskCreated). Requires **new machinery**: `gate-done.sh` checks review-pass + learn-receipt, **not** test evidence, and `state/$sid.json` has no per-task record. TaskCompleted has no matcher and fires on every task — must inspect `task_subject` for the `T-xxx` prefix and `exit 0` otherwise, or it blocks every non-claudehut task. |
| RES-H10 | `type: "prompt"` / `"agent"` hook handlers | 5 | Real; all 13 handlers are `command`. But `gate-done.sh`'s three cheap early exits (`:11`, `:20`, `:45`) mean unengaged sessions cost nothing today — a prompt handler fires on **every** turn end. It has no fail-open equivalent, and `conformance.sh:603` drives the gate by piping JSON into a script, so a prompt handler is **structurally untestable** by the existing harness. Additive advisory only; `type: "agent"` is documented experimental. |
| RES-H5 | `PostCompact` | 5 | **Drop the claimed application** — SessionStart already fires with `source: compact` (`hooks.json:5` already matches it) and, unlike PostCompact, can return `additionalContext`. `inject-phase.sh:23-24` reads only `.phase`/`.profile`. Writing `state/$sid.json` from a hook violates the invariant at `inject-phase.sh:6-7`. Already refuted once at `v0.10.0-verified-plan.md:388`. The only non-redundant niche is `compact_summary` → a telemetry sidecar. |
| RES-H6 | Path-scoped rules are lost at compaction | 3 | Real: docs state rules with `paths:` are "Lost until a matching file is read again". **53 of 55**, not 55 — `vocabulary.md` and `project-structure.md` are unscoped, so the docs' own "always-on anchor" remedy is already shipped. **The enforcement plane does NOT evaporate** — hooks "run as code, not context". What degrades is 53 advisory rule bodies. **Wrong vehicle:** not `inject-phase.sh` (promotes bucket-3 bytes to bucket 1 every turn, and has no post-compaction signal); the right insertion point is `bootstrap.sh`'s compact branch, emitting rule **paths** (tens of bytes), not bodies. |
| RES-H9 | `PostToolBatch` | 5 | Real and blocking-capable, but the hole is largely closed by `reconcile` (serialized `git merge --no-ff`, aborts on conflict / hard-resets on red tests, `bin/claudehut-worktree:107-118`), and implementers write in worktrees **outside** `PROJECT_DIR` (`gate-write.sh:64-65`). No matcher support; would fire after every parallel batch. **Wedge risk unmitigated** — no verified `stop_hook_active` equivalent. Cheaper placement is SubagentStop, already wired and capped. |
| RES-S3 | `allowed-tools` accepts `Bash()` patterns with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` substitution | 2 | Real. But **3 of the 4 named skills are wrong targets**: `discover` and `write-plan` run **bare** `claudehut-state`; `capture-learnings` runs three `scripts/*.sh`; the worktree rule belongs on `implement`, which declares no `allowed-tools` at all. `claudehut-init/SKILL.md:36` needs **two** rules (compound command; each subcommand must match independently). Frame as **ergonomics, not hardening** — `allowed-tools` only grants, so narrowing strictly increases prompting. |
| RES-S4 | `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` in skill bodies | 2 | Only the `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` half is new — `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` is already used in 8 skill bodies including the exact state-file pattern at `review/SKILL.md:83,91`. Legitimate use is **instruction depth**, not tier routing: effort is the user's reasoning budget, the tier is a risk classification (`claudehut-workflow/SKILL.md:49-52`), and `gate-write.sh:110/124/168` would simply deny a wrongly-lowered tier. Hook processes cannot receive skill substitutions. Agent-level `effort:` is already shipped on all 14. |
| RES-S2 | `disable-model-invocation: true` on claudehut-init | 1 (299 B) | **Recommend keep-rejected.** `bootstrap.sh` already runs the generator with the model out of the loop; the flag would break all three eval harnesses' natural-language init phrasings and silently stop stub enrichment (`SKILL.md:39` §2) and MCP suggestions (§3). Hard precondition: `/claudehut:init` **does not exist** (real: `/claudehut:claudehut-init`) — see RES-K5. Already rejected at `v0.10.0-verified-plan.md:403`. |
| RES-S7 | Skill `paths:` glob gate | 1/2 | **Recommend no action.** `bootstrap.sh:95-112` already does the summer-kb install, self-heal and grounding deterministically; the skill's remaining job (`SKILL.md:12-14`) is manual install / explicit refresh / diagnosis — all prompt-driven with no file edit in play, exactly what a `paths` gate would suppress. A glob cannot express "a Gradle file containing `io.f8a.summer`". Whether `paths` even removes a skill from the always-loaded listing is [unverified]. |
| RES-A1 | Agent `maxTurns` | 4 | Real and supported for plugin agents, set on 0 of 14. **Already recorded VERIFIED and rejected** at `v0.10.0-verified-plan.md:520`/`:404` because the docs never state what the parent receives when it fires. Does **not** replace `claudehut-implementer.md:25-26` (that is about returning BLOCKED, not turn count). Two of the three proposed targets are harmful: the implementer runs TDD in a worktree (`v0.10.0-plan-raw.json:46` already said leave it uncapped), and `test-runner` has **no** SubagentStop file contract, so truncation there is a fail-open on the completion gate. Only `claudehut-explorer` (and possibly `reuse-scanner`, which **is** gated) is defensible. |
| RES-P1 | Plugin output style with `force-for-plugin: true` | 1 | The only plugin component that appends arbitrary author prose to the main system prompt (which survives compaction untouched). **Real user-hostile cost:** `plugin.json:24` is `defaultEnabled: true` and the flag "Overrides the user's `outputStyle` setting" with no opt-out short of disabling the plugin; multi-plugin order is nondeterministic. **As written it is a double-pay** — `digest.md:3`, `:7-64` and `:64` already carry the phase rail and REQUIRED NEXT. Only net-neutral-or-better if those come **out** of digest.md and inject-phase.sh in the same commit. Main thread only; reaches none of the 14 agents. Takes effect after `/clear` or a new session. |
| RES-P2 | Plugin `settings.json` `agent` key | — | Real (only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` are supported), and `initialPrompt` is a real frontmatter field. **But `defaultEnabled: true` + "replaces the default Claude Code system prompt entirely" means it rewrites EVERY session in EVERY project.** Overridable by user settings or `--agent`, but most users set neither. Hooks/MCP/CLAUDE.md keep working (the plugin-frontmatter restriction is frontmatter-only). Whether a plugin's own settings.json `agent` resolves its own scoped agents is [unverified]. Prototype behind explicit opt-in, never as a defaultEnabled plugin-root file. |
| RES-P3 | `subagentStatusLine` for the parallel implementer panel | 5 | Real; one of only two supported plugin settings.json keys. **Zero token effect — operator TUI only.** Key the row on `label`/`description` for T-xxx identity, **not** `cwd`: claudehut does not create or name worktrees (`bin/claudehut-worktree` only does status/reconcile/sweep/check-disjoint), so `cwd` is an opaque generated path. Useful payload is `tokenCount`/`contextWindowSize` + `model` + `effort`. Needs CC ≥ 2.1.205 (2.1.214 for `effort`); local is 2.1.233. |

### 6.3 MCP catalog expansion *(prerequisite: PLUMB-F-05's inventory check must land first)*

`templates/mcp-recommendations.md` is **bucket 3** — read on demand by `skills/claudehut-init/SKILL.md:63`, never always-loaded. Agent `tools:` edits are **bucket 4**. Zero main-context cost either way; the win is capability. Note the repo's own v0.10 finding at `v0.10.0-plan-raw.json:185-187`: a catalog row with no consuming agent makes developers pay connection, auth and startup cost for unreachable capability — commit `dfce629` deleted redis and memory for exactly that reason. **Every row below must ship together with its agent frontmatter, or not at all.** `v0.10.0-verified-plan.md:359` also deliberately deferred agent-frontmatter MCP changes to v0.11 with their own eval change — this is that change.

| ID | Server | Add to | Non-negotiable caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP-GRAF | `grafana` (grafana/mcp-grafana, PyPI 1.1.0) | observability-reviewer (`:6`, currently `Read, Grep, Glob` — **zero MCP tools**), perf-reviewer | Ship `--disable-write` **and** `--enabled-tools "datasource,prometheus,loki,pyroscope,dashboard"` (default is ~57 tools). **`--disable-write` disables `find_slow_requests` and `find_error_pattern_logs`** (they create investigations and need the Editor role) — so **drop `find_slow_requests` from the allowlist** and drop "Tempo" from the pitch: it is the only Tempo-touching tool and there is no TraceQL tool. Keep the server named `grafana`. |
| MCP-PROM | `prometheus` (prometheus/prometheus-mcp) | perf-reviewer, observability-reviewer | Default toolset is `all`, which includes **`quit`** (graceful shutdown of Prometheus) and `reload`. **`--mcp.tools=core` alone drops the read tools the reviewers need** (`list_alerts`, `list_rules`, `list_targets`, `tsdb_stats`) — the flag is *additive* on top of core, so use an explicit additive pin with **repeated** flags (`--mcp.tools=list_alerts --mcp.tools=list_rules …`), not kafka's comma form. **Emit on the positive Prometheus signal only — there is no grafana row to gate against and the catalog has no negative-condition mechanism.** Needs a `<PROMETHEUS_URL>` placeholder. |
| MCP-K8S | `kubernetes` (containers/kubernetes-mcp-server) | perf-reviewer, observability-reviewer, reviewer | `--read-only` genuinely removes `pods_exec` (verified in source: `isToolApplicable` filters on `ReadOnlyHint`, which `pods_exec` lacks) — **but it does not bound reads**: `resources_get` has no kind denylist, so Secrets stay readable and `configuration_view` dumps kubeconfig. Upstream pairs it with a dedicated viewer kubeconfig; RBAC is what actually bounds reads. **`--toolsets config,core` is a no-op** (both are already default). `helm_list` needs `--toolsets config,core,helm`. Rename the server to `kubernetes` and use `--scope project`, not upstream's `-s user`. |
| MCP-SENTRY | `sentry` (getsentry/sentry-mcp, remote HTTP + OAuth) | observability-reviewer **only** | Only **9** tools are in `tools/list`, and **7** with the project-scoped URL. `get_issue_details` and `get_event_stacktrace` are **NOT** among them — binding them would be a dead frontmatter name. Bind `search_issues`, `search_events`, `get_sentry_resource`, `execute_sentry_tool`; per-issue detail is reached **through** `execute_sentry_tool`. Two caveats: AI-powered search needs an LLM provider key, and skills gating (`--disable-skills=seer`) can remove Seer. Watch the 90-line agent budget when adding degradation text. |
| MCP-DRYRUN | `dryrun` (boringSQL/dryrun — offline snapshot, **no credentials**) | db-reviewer (`check_migration`, `lint_schema`, `describe_table`, `find_related`) | **Do not copy the 14-name list** — `schema_diff` does not exist (it is `snapshot_diff`), and `explain_query`/`check_drift` are live-only, contradicting the no-credentials thesis. **Gate the perf-reviewer half**: per-node `idx_scan` requires someone to have run `dryrun --profile replicaN snapshot activity`, and claudehut ships no multi-node capture workflow. `--scope project` is genuinely safe here because the offline snapshot puts no secret in a committed `.mcp.json`. |
| MCP-OTEL | `otel` (traceloop/opentelemetry-mcp-server) | perf-reviewer, observability-reviewer | **Drop the grafana-suppression condition** — `find_slow_requests` is a Sift *investigation trigger* requiring the Editor role, disabled under `--disable-write`, and no substitute for `search_traces`/`get_trace`/`list_services`. **Pin a hyphen-free server name** (`otel`), since upstream names it `opentelemetry-mcp`. Half the toolset is LLM-specific and useless here — carry that caveat the way `mcp-recommendations.md:25` carries the RabbitMQ/NATS one. Last **code push** 2026-06-21 (not 2026-08-15 — that is `updated_at`). |
| MCP-MAVEN | `maven-tools` (arvindand/maven-tools-mcp) | brainstormer (`:6` currently `Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch` — zero MCP), security-auditor | **Bucket 2 row, not Bucket 1** — "pom.xml or build.gradle present" fires on every JVM project. **Drop the pom.xml headline**: all 17 real Java repos are `build.gradle` with **zero** `pom.xml`, and the two flagship POM tools require raw POM XML. Only the 9 coordinate tools apply. Not "the only JVM build-tool MCP" — it never invokes Maven, and rnett/gradle-mcp is the genuinely build-tool-shaped alternative. Hyphen hazard: `mcp__maven-tools__resolve-library-id`. |

The genuinely unpinned row **today** is **`github` (`:23`)**, the largest tool-definition sink in the current catalog: add `X-MCP-Toolsets: repos,issues,pull_requests` + `X-MCP-Readonly: true` (or the `/readonly` path). MCP schemas land in the session system prompt, but the cost is conditional on the developer actually running `claude mcp add` — it is not plugin-shipped bytes. |

## 7. Ranked backlog

Ranked by **(token cost + wall-clock pain) × confidence**, with prerequisite chains forced earlier. Not by raw byte count.

**Row 62 is a pointer, not an index entry.** Every item that requires a v0.11 code change has its own row below. Items that were verified and deliberately require **no** edit — keeps, recorded constraints, and levers whose application was narrowed to nothing — are bundled in row 62 and indexed individually in **§3.3** (RES-S5, RES-R1, RES-K1–K5), **§4.6** (KB-1, AGT-1, BKT-1), **§5** (the ST-1 and data-hygiene notes) and **§6.2** (the full lever table, one row per ID with its blocking caveat). Refuted proposals are in **Appendix A**; categories checked and found empty are in **Appendix B**. Nothing is unindexed; row 62 is where the no-action items live.

## 8. What we could not measure

**Rule-load frequency and dispatch mix are [unverified — no ledger data].** Only **2** files across all 15 production repos match `*.rules-loaded.jsonl` or `*.dispatches.jsonl`, both in payment-gateway-ms, because both hook events are new in 0.10.0 and only 2 of 15 installs run it (PLUMB-F-10). **No claim anywhere in this plan about which of the 55 rule files actually load, how often each of the 14 agents is dispatched, or which phase burns the most tokens rests on ledger data.** Every per-rule count in §2 is a glob-match count over the real source tree.

To produce that data, the user runs — in each repo they care about:

```sh
# 1. bring the install up to date (this is the blocker; see PLUMB-F-10)
claude plugin update claudehut

# 2. confirm the v0.10 recorders are wired in the cached copy actually being used
jq -r '.hooks | keys[]' ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claudehut/claudehut/*/hooks/hooks.json \
  | grep -E 'SubagentStart|InstructionsLoaded'

# 3. work normally for a few sessions, then read the ledgers
find ~/Documents/Projects -path '*/claudehut/state/*.rules-loaded.jsonl' -exec cat {} + \
  | jq -r '.file_path' | sed 's#.*/\.claude/rules/##' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
find ~/Documents/Projects -path '*/claudehut/state/*.dispatches.jsonl' -exec cat {} + \
  | jq -r '.agent_type' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# 4. the free native diagnostic, for the cache-miss and long-context flags (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise only)
#    (interactive) /usage
```

Also not determined:

- **The correct `PostToolUseFailure` field for stderr content beyond `.error`** — the Zod validator gives `{error, is_interrupt, duration_ms}` and nothing else; `.error_type` and `.is_timeout` exist only in a stale help blurb. Capture one real payload behind a debug env var before writing any other field path.
- **Whether a fork receives a new `session_id`** — the docs are silent, and this decides whether RES-H3 is a "lost injection" or a "write gate off for the whole session".
- **Whether `bare claudehut-state` resolves** for an installed plugin — this decides whether RES-P6 is a cosmetic cleanup or five live bugs in bucket-1 text.
- **Whether `memory:` on a reviewer auto-enables Write/Edit** (AGT-1) — decides whether extending it is safe.
- **The real semantics of a subagent `worktree` spawned from a properly-installed parent** — the one observed worktree session predates the install by six weeks (see Appendix A).
- **Boot version per repo** — `claudehut-init` never detects it, so RULE-13's `@MockitoBean` claim rests on the plugin's own reference asserting the 3.4 deprecation, not on a measurement. The internal *contradiction* between rule and reference is verified regardless.
- **Session turn counts** — LRN-9's 50-turn / ~109 KB cumulative figure is extrapolated from measured per-turn cost, not observed.
- **Whether any description actually mis-routes in practice** — Claude Code's matcher is not observable from this repo; SKILL-F6/F7/F8 are reasoned from text, and IDEA-R2 is the proposed measurement.
- **Whether merging rules (RULE-14) is safe** — `bin/claudehut-init:191-196` carries `## Learned pitfalls` over only under an unchanged relative path, and no migration path exists.
- **Whether hook `additionalContext` sits before or after a cache breakpoint** — the docs return NOT STATED, so RES-M1 is scoped to byte-nondeterminism and quantifies no cache loss. Likewise NOT STATED: whether a subagent inherits the parent's cache, and whether switching models invalidates it.

## Appendix A — refuted proposals, and why

Recorded so nobody re-proposes them next quarter. Each was checked against primary sources and failed.

| # | Proposal | Refutation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plugin `scope: project` means managed worktrees run with no hooks at all | **Six-week temporal confound.** The cited worktree session ran 2026-07-05→07; claudehut was first enabled at that projectPath 2026-08-15T15:55Z. The transcript shows **zero claudehut agents and zero claudehut skills** too — a not-yet-installed plugin, not a path-resolution gap. The session also *started* at the installed projectPath (hooks fired there) and was moved in mid-session via EnterWorktree. Additionally the proposed remedy names `claudehut-worktree add`, which **does not exist** (verbs are status/check-disjoint/reconcile/sweep; `bin/claudehut-worktree:3` says the managed root is where native `isolation: worktree` creates them). |
| 2 | `asyncRewake` to recover discarded async hook output | The field is real, but the second offered quote ("output is not collected or acted upon") is **inverted** — `hooks.md:3299` says Claude Code *does* deliver `additionalContext` and `systemMessage` from an async hook's JSON on the next turn. The load-bearing premise is false. Would also be a bucket-1 token **cost**. Understates shipped enforcement: `bin/claudehut-state:337-355` already hard-refuses `set-review pass` on unresolved suspects. |
| 3 | `SessionEnd` hook to persist state on normal exit | (a) Plugin-provided hook timeouts **do not raise** the 1.5 s SessionEnd budget. (b) `persist-state.sh` flushes nothing — it `cp`s a file that `bin/claudehut-state:407-411` already wrote synchronously; the snapshot is read only when the live file is **missing** (`bootstrap.sh:31-35`), so a SessionEnd snapshot would never be read. (c) The "terminalSequence" clause is StopFailure's row, not SessionEnd's. |
| 4 | PreToolUse `updatedInput` to rewrite tool calls | **Fabricated verbatim.** The offered "only the fields you include are updated" is the **inverse** of `hooks.md:1714`: "Replaces the entire input object, so include unchanged fields alongside modified ones." A hook written to the offered spec would silently drop every omitted field. |
| 5 | Skill-frontmatter `hooks` with `once: true` to scope the recorders | Chicken-and-egg: skill hooks register **when the skill is invoked**, so a UserPromptExpansion hook in `implement/SKILL.md` can never fire for the prompt that registered it — re-opening the exact slash-invoker wedge `record-skill-expansion.sh:4-9` exists to close. Also inverts three green assertions (`conformance.sh:234-236, 242-244, 245-247`), and mis-scopes `record-rules-loaded.sh` (rules load during Implement, long before Review). Payoff: ~3 fewer process spawns, zero tokens. |
| 6 | Skill `context: fork` + `agent` to collapse brainstorm into its agent | `brainstorm/SKILL.md:14` states the opposite in the file being changed. Its main thread does four things the agent cannot: Write brainstorm.md, two `claudehut-state` Bash writes, and `AskUserQuestion` — and `claudehut-brainstormer.md:6` is `Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch`. The fork also loses the conversation history brainstorm's declared inputs live in. **Evals would stay green while the phase handoff broke.** |
| 7 | Agent `background: true` for the implementer fan-out | Measured and rejected: `BENCH-REPORT.md:19` shows arm A1 (no `background`, what ships) achieved **3/3 concurrency** in headless `-p`; `:20,:26` show A2 at ~56 s vs A1's ~26 s (2× worse); `:67-68` records the user-approved decision rejecting A2 for write tasks; `:104-120` closed the read-only follow-up ("provides NO advantage"). Concurrency comes from batching Agent calls in one message, not from fork mode. |
| 8 | plugin.json `userConfig` | `evals/conformance.sh:95-96` asserts the manifest declares **no** `userConfig`, pinning a documented secrets decision (`10-build-roadmap.md:265`). It is also **per-user and global across all repos** (project settings are ignored), while claudehut is per-project — and `bin/claudehut-init:42-43` already derives the verify command per-repo from real build files. Neither proposed switch exists in `gate-done.sh` or `verify-subagent.sh`. |
| 9 | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` for update-surviving state | Already considered and rejected by name at `07-memory-architecture.md:52` and `09-plugin-structure.md:330`. The documented manifest-diff pattern is **already implemented** at `bootstrap.sh:104-111`. Adopting the per-machine slot would be a **regression**: the KB is service-scoped and one global dir would collide across 15 repos. |
| 10 | Rewrite descriptions to name the action they must PRECEDE | The generalisation is false (5 of 13 superpowers skills have no `before` clause), and the premise is **inverted**: claudehut's phase map is bucket-1 always-loaded (`digest.md:47-57`) and the current phase is re-injected every prompt by a hook (`inject-phase.sh:30-32`), so "in the Implement phase" is the *most* reliably evaluable trigger here. All four named files already carry a non-phase anchor. |
| 11 | Treat ~8 KB as a hard SKILL.md body budget | `lint-prompt-length.sh:22` already sets deliberately calibrated per-skill byte budgets (review 14000, implement 14500, claudehut-workflow 12000), pinned green by `conformance.sh:654-656`. The source's own rule fires only for a skill above 8 KB **with no `references/` directory** — 8 of 10 claudehut skills have one, so **zero** violate it. The proposed extraction of `review/SKILL.md:78-101` would convert an inline read into a mandatory extra file read on a gated path. |
| 12 | Minor findings go to a ledger, never the fix loop | claudehut already has the lane: `review-rigor.md:34-35` (MED blocks unless justified+deferred, LOW advisory) and `:37-38` ("Outstanding = every `✗` at MED+ not yet justified-and-deferred"). A LOW finding never enters `outstanding`. Taken literally ("only MAJOR/CRITICAL re-enter") it would stop MED from blocking — a regression. |
| 13 | Match the corrective form to the failure type | `review/SKILL.md:149-156` is *discipline* guidance, where prohibition + red flags is the prescribed form. review.md's **shape** is specified 27 lines earlier as a positive recipe (`:120-122`) and enforced structurally by four checks in `bin/claudehut-state:316-355`. `claudehut-workflow/SKILL.md:64-65` is already a positive contract row. |
| 14 | A plan-identity ledger trusted over recollection after compaction | **Fabricated verbatim** — the text exists nowhere in obra/superpowers, in any commit (`git log --all -S` returns zero for three phrases). That skill in fact tracks progress with TodoWrite. claudehut also already mirrors T-xxx into the native task list (`write-plan/SKILL.md:4`, `implement/SKILL.md:93`), which is harness-side state that survives compaction. |
| 15 | Guard the session-start injection so subagents ignore it | No dispatched agent ever receives it: `digest.md` has exactly one reader (`bootstrap.sh:59`, SessionStart only, which does not fire for Task-tool subagents), and no agent's `tools:` includes `Skill` or `Task`. Would add ~110 B of permanent bucket-1 cost to guard an event that cannot occur. |
| 16 | `memory:` subagent frontmatter as an unused native capability | Already shipped — `agents/claudehut-learner.md:7` is `memory: project` on main — and already reconciled in the design docs (§1.1 and §6 of `07-memory-architecture.md`). Unshipped risk the proposal omits: `memory:` auto-enables Read/Write/Edit, so adding it to the deliberately write-less reviewer is not free. |
| 17 | `isolation: worktree` for the implementer | Already shipped at `agents/claudehut-implementer.md:9`, with the merge-back decision made at `implement/SKILL.md:77,85-89` and infrastructure in `bin/claudehut-worktree` + `evals/worktree-tests.sh`. The claim's mechanism is also wrong for this repo: claudehut deliberately overrides the default-branch base with `worktree.baseRef=head`, pinned by `conformance.sh:186-188`, `parallel-dispatch-spine-probe.sh:22-24` and `init-tests.sh:161-170`. |
| 18 | `AskUserQuestion` is stripped from subagents, so gates must move to skills | Already implemented in both halves: the principle is stated at `claudehut-workflow/SKILL.md:84` and in the bucket-1 `digest.md:42`; `claudehut-brainstormer.md:6` and `claudehut-planner.md:6` already omit it; and the gates already exist in brainstorm/write-spec/write-plan/claudehut-init. The repo's encoding is **finer** — it branches on "interactive run (AskUserQuestion available)?" with a recorded non-interactive fallback. |
| 19 | Docs name `low` effort for subagents; drop reuse-scanner to `low` | The reuse-scanner **is not dispatched** on `trivial` (`digest.md:51`, `discover/SKILL.md:68-73` — inline, ≤3 greps), so the "fires on a one-line comment fix" impact argument is false. Two green gates pin the opposite (`conformance.sh:324-326` `ultrathink`, `:327-329` `effort: high`). The source itself says `low` suits "non-coding use cases". |
| 20 | Changing effort mid-session invalidates the cache, so put effort in agents/ | Already shipped: all 14 agents carry `effort:` on line 5 (haiku/low test-runner → xhigh planner/security-auditor), pinned by `conformance.sh:327`. The "tempting hook design" it rules out appears not to be a capability — `effort` is a read-only hook **input** field. |
| 21 | Add a PreToolUse hook that filters verbose tool output | The cited page's own remedy for verbose build output is **subagent delegation**, which is claudehut's shipped architecture — every build/test invocation is bucket 4, returning only a summary (`claudehut-test-runner.md:38-39`). The docs' example filter (`\| grep -E '(FAIL\|ERROR)' \| head -100`) emits nothing on a green suite and destroys the pass count, deadlocking `set-review pass`. |
| 22 | `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` is a dead knob; use `effort` | Falsified by its own source: adaptive models ignore **nonzero** budgets, but `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` is live and is the largest thinking-cost lever there is — and subagents inherit the main conversation's thinking config, overriding every `effort:` line. The substitute is also a no-op on 2 of 14 agents (Haiku is absent from the effort-support table). The caveat is already documented at `03-agents.md:94`, and the recommended settings.json does not exist. |
| 23 | Tier-aware model/effort, starting with haiku on the scanners | Already banked by a stronger mechanism: `claudehut-explorer.md:4` and `claudehut-test-runner.md:4` are **already** `model: haiku`; `discover/SKILL.md:68-73` **skips dispatch entirely** on trivial (100% > a downgrade); `review/SKILL.md:65-69` already lets the tier choose the auditor roster; and the fast lane never reaches the opus planner. The stated implementation premise is also wrong — a **per-invocation `model` parameter outranks frontmatter**, so no duplicate agent files are needed. Cold-cache counter-evidence at `v0.10.0-plan-raw.json:408`. |

## Appendix B — categories checked and found empty

Searched, found nothing worth recommending. Recorded so the same searches are not repeated.

**MCP servers that do not exist in usable form.** *Gradle* — IlyaGulya/gradle-mcp-server is the only one with traction (47 stars) and the GitHub API reports `"archived": true`; jermeyyy/gradle-mcp has 1 star. Build invocation stays a Bash concern in `agents/claudehut-test-runner.md`. *Testcontainers* — no server exists; the top search hit is a 4-star .NET Redis demo, and mcp-testcontainers-java (1 star) provides JUnit primitives for testing MCP servers, not a server. *Flyway / Liquibase* — nothing; the search surfaces only unrelated framework-migration tools. The nearest real capability is boringSQL/dryrun's `check_migration` (MCP-DRYRUN). *Pact / consumer-driven contract testing* — SakthikannanSubramanian/pact-contract-mcp has 0 stars; shivangi-975/mcp-pact and hhagenbuch/mcp-pact test MCP servers, not HTTP APIs. Nothing quotable exists for `agents/claudehut-contract-reviewer.md`. *Spring Boot Actuator* — four repos, all unmaintainable: Dmitriusan/mcp-spring-boot-actuator (1 star, archived), sigachev/spring-ops-mcp (1), cpage-pivotal/spring-boot-actuator-mcp-server (0, untouched since 2025-07), thomas-hochbichler/spring-ai-mcp-actuator (0, tutorial code). Recommending one would be the `mcp__postgres__query` error in a new form. *JMX / JVM runtime* — two repos, both 0 stars (thompgt/jvm-mcp-bridge, causaai/jvm-mcp "Sample MCP server", OpenJ9 only).

**MCP servers that exist but solve the wrong problem.** *OpenAPI* — janwilmake/openapi-mcp-server (900), harsha-iiiv/openapi-mcp-generator (630), ivo-toby/mcp-openapi-server (286) and others all turn a spec into callable API tools; **none does spec-versus-spec breaking-change detection**, which is what `claudehut-contract-reviewer` actually needs. That is a genuine gap, not a recommendation. *JetBrains/mcp-jetbrains* (966 stars, active) — dropped because its tools are served by the in-IDE plugin, the proxy repo publishes no tool list, no tool name could be quoted from any doc, and it requires a running IntelliJ a terminal session cannot assume. *pab1it0/prometheus-mcp-server* (511 stars) — superseded by the Prometheus org's own equally-active server (MCP-PROM); recommending a third-party over the project's own would be hard to defend. *`mcp__ide__getDiagnostics`* — supplied by the IDE extension, not a plain Claude Code install; the correct path is the LSP tool (RES-LSP1/LSP2).

**Native fields and settings with no quotable source.** *`maxOutputTokens`* — two fetches of the settings docs returned no row for this key, so no verbatim exists and no claim is made that it exists. *`claudeMdExcludes`* and *`autoMemoryDirectory`* — documented and unused, but no concrete claudehut file would change or benefit, so they stay out rather than becoming speculative. *Agent `disallowedTools`* — real and unused, but the read-only reviewers already use positive `tools:` allowlists that exclude Write/Edit, and it removes tools, not shell capabilities, so it closes no Bash-redirection path. *Agent `initialPrompt`* — real, but applies only when the agent runs as the main session agent, so it is folded into RES-P2 rather than standing alone. *MCP `alwaysLoad: true`* and the `plugin:<plugin>:<server>` scoped name — real, but claudehut ships no `.mcp.json` by deliberate design; actionable only after a product decision to bundle servers. *Claude Code `Workflow` tool* — real, but `review/SKILL.md` and `claudehut-workflow/SKILL.md` already orchestrate the auditor fan-out; swapping to a workflow script is a rewrite, not an improvement.

**Deprecations that would break claudehut: none found.** A search of the hooks docs for deprecated/removed/renamed events and fields returned nothing. The only deprecation encountered anywhere is the standalone `/output-style` command (deprecated v2.1.73, removed v2.1.91), which claudehut does not use. The two breakage-class findings that *are* in this plan (RES-X1, RES-X2) come from **sandboxing**, not deprecation.

**Repos not opened, and why.** Aggregator/marketplace collections with high star counts — alirezarezvani/claude-skills (24,538), hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code (52,448), jeremylongshore/claude-code-plugins-plus-skills (2,647), rohitg00/awesome-claude-code-toolkit (2,520), davila7/claude-code-templates — are repackaged bulk lists, not authored patterns; star count there measures list popularity, not design quality. obra/superpowers-skills (737) reports `"archived": true`; obra/superpowers `main` was read instead. disler/claude-code-hooks-mastery was skipped after RES-K1 established from primary evidence that claudehut's 13-command / 11-event hook layer already leads the comparison set. anthropics/skills `spec/agent-skills-spec.md` is an 87-byte stub redirecting to an external site with no normative content; `skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md` was used instead. **An MCP integration pattern worth adopting was found in none of the repositories opened** — reporting one would have required citing a file that was not read.

**One first-party ceiling claudehut passes.** `anthropics/skills skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:96` states "Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines". All claudehut skills are 56–162 lines. The byte-based pressure discussed at RES-S5 and Appendix A #11 has a different (Codex) provenance and is stated as such.
